readback_body:
## Requirements: Nession Pages — AI Collaboration Space / Engineering Observatory

### Background / product outcome

Nession is not only a distributed Terminal / Agent workspace; its own development is becoming an **Issue-centric, multi-Agent collaborative engineering process** (#1664). Today project documentation, repository metrics, Agent workflow execution, Issue/PR progress, Acceptance/E2E proof and orphan Run Store information are scattered across README, GitHub Actions, Issues/PRs and orphan branches.

Build an **independent public GitHub Pages site** as Nession's project homepage and a readable, evidence-backed window into **how Nession is built with AI Agents**.

**North-star question:** A visitor opening the site should be able to answer: *What is Nession? What are its AI Agents working on? How is the project progressing? What engineering evidence backs the reported progress?*

**This is a public, read-only project and collaboration showcase, not the authenticated Nession Web workspace, an operational Grafana replacement, or a privileged controller.** The home page starts with the product/work narrative, not a wall of monitoring cards, consistent with `VISION.md` and `PRINCIPLE.md`.

### Information architecture and UX

Suggested stable routes (implementation may use a Pages-safe routing strategy):

| Surface | Main question | Minimum content |
|---|---|---|
| **Home / Overview** (`/`) | What is Nession, and what is happening now? | Product proposition, concise architecture/use cases, GitHub / Docs / Install links; collaboration loop diagram (Issue → Developer → Reviewer → CI/E2E → Acceptance → Merge); latest activity and top-level project pulse |
| **AI Agents** (`/agents`) | Who does the work, with what outcome? | Agent role roster (developer/reviewer/acceptor/auditor), stable **registered AI Agent** identities and provider/model *only if safe to disclose*, latest observed run/status, 7d/30d run counts, duration, tokens, observed cost, tools/skills/MCP usage, fail/retry/recovery coverage |
| **Work / Collaboration** (`/work`) | Which Issues/PRs are active, and where are they stuck? | Linked open/active Issues and PRs; responsible role, workflow stage, CI/Review/E2E/SC Acceptance state, last activity and evidence links; clickable Issue → PR → Agent run/attempt → test/review/acceptance drilldown; activity timeline with source links |
| **Repository** (`/repository`) | How healthy and active is the codebase? | Reuse Repository Metrics vs Engineering Efficiency hierarchy: source/test/protocol inventory, Rust/Web coverage, test health, commits/churn/Issue/PR/Workflow throughput, clearly labeled current and rolling 7d/30d windows |
| **Run Stores / Evidence** (`/evidence`) | Where is the collaboration history and how trustworthy is it? | **Metadata-only** inventory of `metrics`, `acceptance-results`, `task-results` and **`agent-store` only once it actually exists**; purpose/owner, update time, allowed public record counts, schema/lineage, trustworthy status of source validation/integrity audit, links to safe source evidence |

Information is progressive: summary → focused view → source provenance. Default views prioritize **ongoing work and recent evidence**, with search/filter (role, provider, Issue/PR, time range, status) where useful. Pages owns an **entirely independent visual language and UI/UX system** (typography, colors, spacing, iconography, layout, motion, responsive rules, dark/light and empty/error states). Static routes must support direct deep links and refresh on GitHub Pages.

**Two different meanings of Agent must never be conflated:**

- **AI Workflow Agents**: GitHub Actions / Provider-native developer, reviewer, acceptance, auditor roles, with stable `(repo, role, agent_id, issue)` identities and distinct logical Agent / Slice / run / attempt / Provider-session concepts (#1664). This is the **primary** Agents screen.
- **Nession runtime node Agents**: server-registered hosts running `nession-agent` / tmux sessions. These belong to the Nession product runtime; **do not derive their real-time online state from GitHub Workflow Agents**. A public runtime overview is optional and opt-in, displaying only explicitly sanitized aggregates from a separately authorized source; otherwise mark unavailable or omit it. Never expose private host/session inventories.

### Existing sources and ownership: consume, do not duplicate

| Data | Source of truth / owner | Pages responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Repository inventory, coverage and throughput | #1210, #1240; existing `metrics` branch `metrics.json` | Read validated snapshots and present them; do not re-implement metric collection |
| AI Agent summary and usage | #1664, #1692; trusted `metrics` run summaries / normalized execution traces / derived `agent-metrics.json` | Display observed coverage and normalized metrics; no raw tool/prompts/transcripts |
| Agent efficiency / cost analysis | #1737 deterministic analyzer | Reuse its pinned report or a compatible sanitized derived projection; do not introduce different attribution formulas |
| Work, Reviews, CI, Issue/PR status | Canonical GitHub Issues/PRs/Actions and #1664 state/Outbox evidence | Join using authenticated Issue/PR refs, run+attempt and exact SHA; no parallel collaboration state machine |
| SC Acceptance and E2E | #1649, #1474, #1702, #1728 and `acceptance-results` | Read trusted verdicts at the applicable SHA; never infer Pass from a comment, a workflow name or a stale run |
| Orphan governance / audit | #1690, #1730, #1742; authoritative branch-specific owners | Show only verified safe metadata, audit result and provenance; do not treat a branch's existence or a successful writer test as enforced immutability |

Example drilldown:

```text
Issue #N (declared SC / required E2E)
   └─ PR #M (head SHA, review / checks)
       ├─ Developer role → Agent ID → Slice → GitHub run/attempt
       ├─ Reviewer role  → result / repair / resumed run
       └─ CI / selected E2E / Acceptance
           └─ trusted source evidence / durable record reference
```

The graph must show only relationships provable by canonical IDs/evidence. Missing or ambiguous links are **Unlinked / Unknown**, not guessed.

### Standalone Pages project (hard boundary)

**Nession Pages and `web/` are two independent applications with different users, security domains and release lifecycles. Pages MUST NOT be implemented under `web/`, including `web/src`, `web/public`, `web/dist`, Web router/menu, or the Web deployment artifact.** Pages must not alter the authenticated workspace's routing or bundle.

Use a dedicated repository-root `pages/` project as the default ownership boundary:

```text
nession/
├── web/                      # Nession product UI / authenticated workspace (unchanged)
├── pages/                    # Public project & AI collaboration site (independent application)
│   ├── package.json          # Independent build/scripts/dependencies
│   ├── src/                  # Home, Agents, Work, Repository, Evidence
│   ├── public/               # Static assets (only public-safe assets)
│   └── ...                   # Independent config/lockfile and generated output
├── e2e/tests/pages-*.spec.ts # Shared E2E framework, but tests target standalone Pages origin
└── .github/workflows/        # Dedicated trusted Pages build/publish workflow
```

- The **only shared boundaries** are non-UI foundations: versioned read-only public data contracts, authenticated GitHub source APIs, and repository-level E2E/Gates. **No design tokens, theme, stylesheet, UI library/wrappers, icons, assets, component implementations, React hooks or application code may be imported or copied from `web/` or from packages whose UI design is owned by `web/`. No reverse dependencies.**
#### Independent Pages design system (non-negotiable)

Nession Pages has its **own design brief and visual identity**, authored specifically for a public project introduction and AI collaboration observatory. **Do not copy, extend, import, extract or imitate the product `web/` design system**; merely putting copied tokens/components under `pages/` does not satisfy isolation.

- All Pages-specific color palettes, typography scales, spacing, grids, radii, elevations, iconography, illustration style, information density, micro-interactions and responsive layouts are **chosen and maintained under `pages/`**. Its pages, charts, cards, tables, filters and navigation are designed and implemented independently.
- **Do not import or copy** `web/` CSS, Tailwind config/theme, tokens, Storybook/shadcn-installed component source, application React components, component wrappers, icons, shared UI hooks or visual assets. Do not add any dependency pointing to `web/` or Web-owned design packages.
- Third-party UI/visualization libraries may be selected independently for Pages if needed, but their usage/configuration must be defined within `pages/`; no implicit design-system coupling through monorepo aliases or shared root styles.
- Referencing `VISION.md`, `PRINCIPLE.md` and brand/product facts informs **editorial content and product messaging only**, not a mandate to reuse Web's styles, tokens or patterns. The public-facing site is intentionally allowed to have a different visual treatment.
- Review/CI must verify package dependencies, imports/aliases, CSS/assets and build graph; a new dependency or path allowing Pages → Web UI ownership is a **blocking violation**, even when the resulting screenshot looks acceptable.

- Pages has its own build command, static assets, routing base path, GitHub Pages artifact and deployment workflow. It must build and deploy **without building `web/`**; product Web must independently build and deploy without `pages/`.
- Pages is a public, anonymous **snapshot reader**. It does not connect to Nession Server's private WebSocket, reuse the product Web's access token/auth, or call live management APIs. Public projection is generated by a trusted server-side/CI step, not by shipping a privileged client API key.
- A failure to build or publish Pages must not block or redeploy the product Web; a Web build/runtime failure must not block a Pages-only update. **Data contracts may be shared; visual design, UI components and styles may not.**
- Keep `pages/` changes explicitly isolated in PR/review scope; modifications to `web/` require a distinct separately justified requirement/PR. This standalone boundary is an **Acceptance invariant**, not an implementation preference.

### Static publication, data contract, freshness

1. Keep all Pages application source inside the independent root-level **`pages/`** project, with its own build dependencies, **standalone design system**, and deploy artifact (see hard boundary above). Never place Pages application files under `web/` or bundle them with the authenticated workspace. Reuse only non-UI public data contracts; **never reuse or extract `web/` design assets**. Deploy using trusted main-owned GitHub Pages Actions; generated site/data **must not commit counters to `main`**.
2. A **trusted read-only public projection builder** consumes versioned source snapshots from existing stores and GitHub's read APIs. Produce bounded, deterministic, strictly allowlisted `public-pages.json` (or versioned per-section JSON) as part of the Pages artifact. Include `schema_version`, `generated_at`, `source_main_sha`, per-source ref/SHA/run/attempt/time, measured window, availability/error/freshness and source links. Do not create another orphan store or Writer/SC projector.
3. Reuse scheduled/manual refresh cadence (initial target: **every 4 hours**, coordinated with metrics publication) and deploy on **site-source change**; avoid a new high-frequency workflow on every code push. Ensure each refresh uses a consistent **pinned** `metrics`/evidence ref and bounded GitHub pagination. Initial publication must work with no Agent data. Do not fetch privileged APIs or embedded tokens from the public browser.
4. If a producer or source is missing, stale, rate-limited or fails schema/integrity validation, keep last-known-good safe data with an explicit stale/error banner **or** render unavailable; never publish fabricated zeros, current status, empty successful results or false 'online' state. A successful Pages deployment does not imply all upstream workflows passed.
5. Security: publish **only an allowlisted projection**, never raw orphan files, encrypted checkpoint blobs, Provider-native sessions, prompts, tool arguments/results, private traces, environment values, tokens, IPs, private hostnames, local paths, session identifiers, privileged audit artifacts or any secret. Validate untrusted Issue/PR/title/Markdown content and external links; escape HTML/JS; cap text/cardinality and protect against XSS, prototype/path injection and accidental PII. Any future private data view requires a different authenticated surface.
6. Orphan protection must be described honestly: until #1690 demonstrates live server-side authorization and independent anchored integrity evidence, show **Not verified / Partial** for those guarantees; Pages cannot self-certify trusted integrity from data in the same branch. No public force-push/re-root of existing Run Store history for this site.

### Delivery boundaries / staged implementation

- **Phase 1 (MVP):** branded Pages Home + AI Agent roster/usage + Repository metrics + active Issue/PR list; real generated public snapshots, timestamps, backlinks and graceful missing data; README links to Pages.
- **Phase 2 (traceable collaboration):** evidence-backed Issue ↔ PR ↔ run/attempt ↔ Review/SC/E2E views, Agent activity timeline and efficiency trends; join only supported canonical evidence.
- **Phase 3 (store transparency):** orphan store inventory, safe per-store lineage and independently verified integrity/audit statuses; optional runtime-node **aggregate** overview only if a safe authoritative source is provided.

This single Issue owns the public **presentation and export interface**. Additional source collection, SC orchestration, telemetry ingestion, Provider runtime, encryption or authorization gaps stay with their existing owner Issues; break large implementation PRs into reviewable slices without duplicating ownership.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 A public, unauthenticated GitHub Pages URL presents Nession's purpose, architecture, install/repo links and the Issue-centric AI collaboration loop; README points to it.
- [ ] SC-02 Public Pages is a **standalone root `pages/` application with a fully independent visual design system**, never `web/`: independent package/build/deploy artifact, routes, typography/tokens/theme/icons/components/assets, no `web/` or Web-owned UI package imports/copies, and mobile/desktop, dark/light, deep-link refresh, accessibility and empty/error states work.
- [ ] SC-03 AI Workflow Agent roles/IDs/providers and **actual observed** per-run/rolling token, duration, usage and cost metrics display with observation coverage; logical Agent, Slice, run/attempt and runtime node Agent are never conflated.
- [x] SC-04 Repository view reuses #1210/#1240 canonical metrics and reports source SHA, timestamps and measurement windows without inventing formulas or a new collector.
- [x] SC-05 Active Issues/PRs show source links, true current GitHub state and meaningful progress; unknown Owner/Stage is explicit rather than guessed.
- [x] SC-06 Issue → PR → Agent run/attempt → Review/CI/E2E/Acceptance drilldown only displays provable exact-SHA relationships; stale proof never appears as current Pass.
- [ ] SC-07 Orphan view inventories only **actually existing** known stores with their canonical purpose, source lineage, safe counts/freshness and audit status; no fabricated `agent-store` data or unverified 'immutable/secure' label.
- [ ] SC-08 Public export is versioned, deterministic, pin-ref/source-traceable, schema-validated, bounded and completely **read-only** relative to the canonical stores; no new telemetry writer/SC projector or site-generated commit on `main`.
- [ ] SC-09 Scheduled/manual refresh and trusted Pages deployment work with scoped permissions; no secret or authenticated runtime API is shipped to the browser; stale/missing/failed sources show truthful state.
- [ ] SC-10 Security fixtures reject raw Agent transcript/prompt/tool payloads, checkpoint bytes, tokens, private IP/path/hostname/session data, malicious Issue content and unsafe URLs before publication.
- [ ] SC-11 Deterministic fixture tests verify grouping, zero-vs-null, exact-SHA joins, mixed versions, missing Agent data, duplicate/out-of-order runs, paginated Issues/PRs, source drift and safe partial failure.
- [ ] SC-12 End-to-end browser checks cover key Pages views, route refresh, responsive layout, safe rendering and source deep links; Quality Gate and PR-head Acceptance retain their existing ownership.
- [x] SC-13 Existing README SVG/JSON metrics, Agent ingest, orphan write authorization and authenticated product `web/` routing/build/deployment continue unaffected; independent Pages and Web builds/deployments succeed without invoking each other. Automated dependency/style-source checks confirm no Pages UI, design, CSS, asset or component dependency on `web/`.
